description: Two-part printed box for the assembled RF433 bridge carrier board (62 x 60 mm) with a DOIT ESP32 DevKit v1 (30-pin, USB-C), whose USB end overhangs the carrier by about 7 mm, and a CC1101 module that overhangs its right edge. The tray holds the board on four M3 insert standoffs, has a USB window and an open-topped slot for the SMA jack so the antenna stays outside and can point vertically, and optional floor holes for wall or shelf fixing; the plain lid clamps the board with four screws and leaves the Wi-Fi antenna end clear.

hardware.notes: St-John-Software/electronics, hardware/rf433-bridge/; 62 x 60 mm with a DOIT ESP32 DevKit v1 (30-pin, USB-C), whose USB end overhangs the carrier by about 7 mm, and an E07-M1101D soldered on
One per standoff; set insert_hole_d to 2.6 instead for self-tapping screws
Through a lid boss into its standoff insert
Optional: countersunk floor fixing to a wall or shelf (floor_fixings)
As fitted to the board; its elbow turns it vertical outside the box. A straight antenna needs an optional SMA right-angle adapter.

printing_notes: Print both parts as exported without supports: the base floor-down, the lid outer-face-down.
Press the four M3 heat-set inserts into the standoffs before fitting the board.
Fit the antenna before power-up (board safety note): drop the board in with the SMA jack into the wall slot, screw the antenna on outside, then fit the lid and the four screws.
To fix the box to a wall or shelf, screw the empty tray down through the two floor holes before fitting the board.

The fit uses the devkit and CC1101 overhangs caliper-measured on the assembled board (devkit USB-C face 8.3 mm and module 5.9 mm past the carrier edges); the 0.1.0 base does not fit this board, so reprint the base. Devkit and module heights and screw_l are still design values: check them on this print.
wall, floor_t, corner_r, standoff_h and above_pcb are shared parameters: set them identically on the base and the lid.
